_provenance.label: real dunkai output, schema v2, first capture with interface taxonomy routing
_provenance.purpose: New baseline for the comparison series. Measures downstream Phase 5 error counts with Power and the wireless interfaces no longer scored as part requirements, and each retained requirement tagged with its relationship type.

replaces_v1_v4_series.decision: This fixture, not dunkai_real_v1..v4, is the comparison point going forward.
why: The v1-v4 captures were all built from a 'panic-button profile' that was never committed and did not survive a machine move. The fixtures record its OUTPUT and describe it in prose ('2 push buttons, 3 status LEDs'), but the requirements JSON that produced them is gone, so none of them can be re-run for a matched before/after comparison.

Their own provenance already caveats them: 'Three captures of one profile is a small sample. Error counts move with architecture shape as much as with ranking quality.' and 'Architecture agent is non-deterministic; this is one sample.'
v1 is schema 1.0 (nets carry `connections`, not `members`) and was already outside the comparable set.

This capture is generated from ai_engine/data/profiles/env-sensor-node.json, which IS committed, so it can be re-run. The profile deliberately spans I2C, SPI, UART and GPIO so more than one retrieval path is exercised.
replaces_v1_v4_series.cost_acknowledged: Retiring v3/v4 loses the before/after pair that measured the verified-pin-coverage and verified-absence-ceiling changes. That pair was already unreproducible; the loss is of a weak baseline, not a trustworthy one.

endpoint_role_states.settled_null: UART (peer) carries endpoint_role: null -- terminal, no controller concept exists
endpoint_role_states.not_yet_computed: I2C/SPI (shared_bus) and GPIO (not_a_bus) OMIT the key entirely
endpoint_role_states.not_applicable: Power dropped before retrieval; recorded in interfaces_not_applicable

architecture_drift.warning: The architecture agent remains non-deterministic. This run assigned U1=MCU, whereas the pre-change run of the SAME profile assigned U2=MCU, with different shortlist sizes per role. Error counts therefore move with architecture shape as well as with ranking behaviour, exactly as the v1-v4 provenance warned. A single capture on either side is not a controlled measurement of the taxonomy change.

known_caveats: eda.py parse_bom_csv calls the live EasyEDA API per BOM row; packages are not offline-reproducible.
One capture per side. The architecture agent is non-deterministic, so the before/after delta below is indicative, not a controlled measurement.

The published v4 by-code split (PIN_NOT_FOUND 4 / PART_CAPABILITY_MISMATCH 1) does NOT reproduce on pcb-agent c5fa8db: the totals still reproduce exactly (phase3=9, phase5=5) but the split is now PART_CAPABILITY_MISMATCH 3 / PIN_NOT_FOUND 2. pcb-agent has since changed how curated pinouts claim padCount, which moves errors between exactly these two codes. Compare totals across the v-series, not the split.

before_after_same_profile.headline: NO CHANGE. Taxonomy routing did not move any downstream Phase 5 count.

part_selection.renumbered_only: CAP200DG-TL, MC9S08DZ32ACLC and ESP-M1 all appear in both runs, permuted across U1/U2/U3 by architecture node ordering -- not a selection change.
genuinely_changed: U5 MCP9700T-E/LT -> MCP9700T-E/TT (same MPN, different package suffix)

before_after_same_profile.why_no_movement: Consistent with the measured evidence scarcity: 97% of candidates carry no structured interface attribute and 89% are absent from the 156-part pin-coverage table, so interface_match returns the same no-evidence constant for nearly every candidate either way. Removing Power from the required set changes each score MAGNITUDE but rarely the ORDER, because Power scored identically across candidates within a pool. The change is correct and removes a whole class of meaningless work, but the leverage on downstream errors lies in the two deferred phases (quantity-aware matching for GPIO/PWM/ADC/CS) and in catalogue evidence coverage -- not here.
